description: Compile an OpenQASM program through named passes (lowering, checked rewrites, phase folding, one- and two-qubit resynthesis, and every rotation off the multiples of π/4 written as a Clifford+T word within its share of the ε budget), each checked where it acts. Returns the compiled program and a certificate sealed with the service's key: each pass's counts before and after, its check and verdict (proof, exact or approximate with its distance), the budget and the bound the distances add to. verify_quantum_receipt checks it. Quote the bound; an approximate compile is not exact. A large or very fine compile is refused with the local command.

basis.description: clifford_t (default): every rotation off the multiples of π/4 written as a Clifford+T word within its share of epsilon; standard: nothing approximated.

epsilon.description: The most the output may differ from the program in the operator norm, up to a global phase, shared by its rotations (default 1e-6).

level.description: 0: lower and approximate; 1 (default): also checked rewrites and phase folding; 2: also one- and two-qubit resynthesis.

name: compile_qasm

anyOf.description: A compile as a host returns it (the command line's compile --json, both servers' compile_qasm, the job service's POST /v1/compile): the request as given, and the result, which its receipt seals in the form every job's receipt takes. The result holds the compiled program and its certificate (wai.quantum.compile/1): each pass's counts before and after, its check and verdict, the budget and the bound the passes' distances add to. A result names the engine that made it and this schema (engine and schema); results made before results carried them have neither.

request.description: The program and the compile's options, as given.

dd.description: Dynamical decoupling in each window where a qubit idles long enough: xx or xy4 (or {"sequence": …}), checked to change nothing without noise.

twirl.description: Twirl each two-qubit Clifford gate with Paulis drawn from a seeded stream: true (seed 1), or {"seed": N}. One seed is one instance, checked to be the same circuit.

certificate.description: What the compile did and how each step was checked. Hashes are BLAKE3, in hex, of the program as read (written out as OpenQASM 3) and of the output text.

epsilon.description: The budget, the bound the passes' distances add to, and how the budget was shared among the rotations.

counts.description: A circuit's counts, as the compiler counts them.

passes.description: Each pass: its name, the counts before and after, and its check (how, the verdict, and its distance where it has one).

after.description: A circuit's counts, as the compiler counts them.

before.description: A circuit's counts, as the compiler counts them.

component.description: Beside a registered pass's record: its identity. Its check is the engine's, on the whole circuit (by: engine).

certified.description: Beside a registered component: the engine does not certify it.

digest.description: BLAKE3 of the component's descriptor in its canonical JSON (engine::registry::digest_of).

origin.description: built-in: the engine's own; registered: a host's own, added in its process, not part of the engine.

reading.description: What the certificate says of the output, in words.

rotations.description: Each rotation written as a Clifford+T word: its angle, its T count, its distance.

counts.description: A circuit's counts, as the compiler counts them.

whole.description: The check of the whole output against the whole program, where it was made.

components.description: The identity of every component that made the compile, when a registered pass took part (engine::registry): the program's format and each pass, each registered one marked so.

items.description: One component that made the result (engine::registry): its kind, name and version, the BLAKE3 digest of its descriptor, and whether it is built in. A result carries these only when a registered component took part; one made by built-ins alone names them as it always has (its method, its compile's passes, its noise's channels and the engine's version), the digests of that version listed by the components list.

certified.description: Beside a registered component: the engine does not certify it.

digest.description: BLAKE3 of the component's descriptor in its canonical JSON (engine::registry::digest_of).

origin.description: built-in: the engine's own; registered: a host's own, added in its process, not part of the engine.

engine.description: The engine that made the result: the wai-quantum crate's name and version.

options.description: The options the compile ran with, the defaults filled in.

receipt.description: A result's receipt: an Ed25519 signature, by the key it names, over digest = BLAKE3("wai:quantum-service-receipt\x02" ‖ len ‖ request ‖ len ‖ result), each of request and result in its RFC 8785 canonical text (the result without its receipt member), each length 8 bytes big-endian. Whatever members the request and the result hold are sealed, the result's engine and schema among them. The first receipts (no canon member, $defs/first) sealed their writer's compact text under the domain ending \x01; they still verify. wai/extensions/quantum-providers.md section 8.2 states the seal in full, and section 8.4 what a verifier checks.

canon.description: The canonical form the digest is taken over.

digest.description: The digest signed, 32 bytes in lower-case hex.

key.description: The signing key, 32 bytes in lower-case hex.

signature.description: The signature, 64 bytes in lower-case hex.

receipt.title: wai.quantum.receipt/2

stages.description: With stages: the circuit after each pass.

verdict.description: How far the engine checked an answer about a program, as one level of an ordered ladder (wai-quantum://docs/verdicts): refused, parsed, executed, evidence, proof. A level says how far the engine checked, not that the answer is good: holds says whether the intents held (true, false, or null when none was decided). A job's result carries one under verdict when the job gives an intent or asks for one, and the receipt seals it; both MCP servers state one beside every answer about a program.

critique.description: The program's smells, each with its lines.

executed.description: The method that ran and its accuracy class, and the distance a compile put between the program and what ran.

items.description: One intent's check: what it asked, whether it held, how strong the check was and how it was made.

distribution.description: The program's distribution, when its outcomes are few enough to list.

fit.description: A sampled intent: the test, its statistic, degrees of freedom and p-value, the level, and whether it rejected.

impossible.description: The outcomes sampled that the stated distribution gives probability 0: the first 64, in order.

impossible_outcomes.description: How many outcomes sampled the stated distribution gives probability 0.

method.description: A sampled intent: the method the samples were run by.

outcomes.description: The outcomes the distribution holds, or the samples' distinct outcomes.

parsed.description: Whether the reader took the program, and its warnings and notes with their codes, or its refusal.

items.description: One of the reader's diagnostics: its code, what happens to the construct it is about, its message (without the line or the code), and where it stands.

text.description: The refusal as the reader wrote it, with its line and code.

rank.description: The level's place on the ladder, from 0 (refused) to 4 (proof).

refusal.description: For a refused job: its message and its codes.

repairs.description: Each edit a repair made, with the code it answered and the lines it changed.

statement.description: The level in one plain line.
